events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 6 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (12:54:00 → 12:55:40), i.e. within the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so no cancellation fee could arise on RydeX. [F2] [NS-0 NS-4]
C2: The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival, so NS-1 requirement (i) is not met and the $6.61 rider no-show fee cannot stand. [F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C3: At the moment of cancellation the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2138 m and he never came within 200 m, so NS-1 requirement (ii) (driver at the pickup point when arrival is indicated) is not met either. [F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The timeline shows driver_arrived_at is null — the platform itself never recorded the driver at the pickup point — so the driver's written "I was on my way" statement cannot cure the missing arrival record. [F3 F8] [NS-1 NS-2 NS-0]
C5: The $6.61 cancellation fee appears on the fare records with no surge (1.0×) and no published additional item supporting it; since the charge fails NS-1/NS-4 it must be refunded in full. [F2 F5 F6] [NS-2 NS-4 NS-7 FARE-1]
C6: Flags for account review: the driver indicated no arrival and the platform recorded no arrival, yet a no-show cancellation fee was still charged to the rider; this pattern is on record in this case as the fee was levied without the NS-1 preconditions. [F3 F4 F5] [NS-2]

Asks: refund_full $6.61

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.96)
events.body:
The case is a rider-initiated cancellation on a RydeX booking, so it enters only through NS-0's rider branch: cancelled_by = rider [F2], and the fee can only be tested under NS-4, not under the driver no-show provisions [F2][NS-0]. The trace settles that the rider cancelled 100 seconds after acceptance (12:54:00 → 12:55:40) [F2], which is inside the 3-minute free-cancellation window of NS-4, so no $6.61 cancellation fee could arise on this trip [F2][NS-4].

Independently, no arrival-based charge exists on this record: driver_arrived_at is null [F3], the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival [F4], and the closest approach to the pickup was 2138 m, never within 200 m [F1]. NS-1(i) and NS-1(ii) therefore both fail [F4][F1][NS-1], and where NS-1 fails the fee must be refunded in full under NS-2 [F2][NS-2]. The driver's written "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F8] is a statement, not a system record, and cannot cure the missing arrival record; the platform records [F3][F4] control.

The amount follows the trace formula: the cancellation fee on the fare record is $6.61 [F5], with surge 1.0× so nothing else attaches [F6]; 1 × $6.61 = $6.61 [F5][F6][NS-4]. That single fee is the contested item, so it is refunded in full [F5][NS-7].

No account flag attaches: NS-2's flag requires a driver who tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, and here no tap occurred at all [F2][F4][NS-2]. The rider's two prior upheld no-show disputes [F12] and the driver's clean record [F13] are profile facts and decide nothing [F12][F13][NS-0].

Safety screen: I read every message in the file — the complaint (driver "nowhere near", a lateness objection) and the driver's statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F8] — plus the absence of any chat [F7]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and no safety issue is in dispute [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. Evidence suffices: the timeline and fare records settle both the NS-4 timing and the NS-1 preconditions [F2][F4][F5].

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching, NS-4 would have upheld the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (12:54:00 → 12:55:40), i.e. within the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so no cancellation fee could arise on RydeX.
The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival, so NS-1 requirement (i) is not met and the $6.61 rider no-show fee cannot stand.

At the moment of cancellation the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2138 m and he never came within 200 m, so NS-1 requirement (ii) (driver at the pickup point when arrival is indicated) is not met either.

The timeline shows driver_arrived_at is null — the platform itself never recorded the driver at the pickup point — so the driver's written "I was on my way" statement cannot cure the missing arrival record.
The $6.61 cancellation fee appears on the fare records with no surge (1.0×) and no published additional item supporting it; since the charge fails NS-1/NS-4 it must be refunded in full.

Flags for account review: the driver indicated no arrival and the platform recorded no arrival, yet a no-show cancellation fee was still charged to the rider; this pattern is on record in this case as the fee was levied without the NS-1 preconditions.

weaknesses: The complaint frames the cancellation as justified by the driver being "nowhere near", but NS-4/NS-8 give the rider no free-cancellation right for driver lateness; the rider's own cancellation is the factual trigger of the fee, so the rider must rely entirely on the fee-liability defects (F2, F4) rather than on the driver's lateness.
The rider's 90-day history shows 2 disputes with 2 upheld (both no-show) (F12), which the other side may use to argue habit/credibility, though profile facts cannot decide the case.

The driver's statement (F8) is unrebutted by any rider message — there is no chat record at all (F7) — so the driver may argue the rider never contacted him; however the system records (F1, F3, F4) outweigh the statement.

claims.assertion: The cancellation fee is not a no-show fee at all: the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (F2), so the case falls under NS-4, not NS-1/NS-6, and no waiting-fee or no-show entitlement on my side is in issue.

NS-4 does not charge a fee within 3 minutes of matching; because the rider cancelled at 1:40 after acceptance (F2), the statutory precondition 'cancelled after 3 minutes of matching' for the $6.61 is absent, so the fee should be refunded in full.

Ryde has published no rule making the fee unavailable to the rider merely because the driver had not yet arrived, so lateness to the pickup cannot convert this early cancellation into a chargeable one.

I never pressed 'I'm Here' and the platform recorded no automatic arrival (F4, F3), so no waiting-time entitlement or arrival-based fee can be claimed by me — the rider's money should not be retained on that basis.

My GPS closest approach was 2,138 m from the pickup point and I never came within 200 m (F1); this is a fact in my favour only in that it proves I never claimed arrival — it does not excuse a fee that the policy does not authorise.

This is a fare/fee-authorisation dispute only: nothing in the record supports a safety escalation, as there is no chat at all and my only written words were 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled' (F7, F8).
My account record is clean — 5.0 years, 4.76 rating, 649 trips in 90 days and 0 upheld disputes — so no account flag or fraud finding against me is warranted in this case.

weaknesses: The rider's profile shows 2 disputes in 90 days and 2 upheld (F12), which supports the rider's credibility and cuts against any suggestion that this complaint is opportunistic; the judge may read the same fact as a pattern against riders, but it is honestly adverse to me here.

The rider's complaint asserts the driver was 'nowhere near' — the GPS fact F1 (2,138 m, never within 200 m) confirms the rider's version of the approach, so I cannot contest that part of the narrative, and it is the fact the other side will lead with.

My own written statement F8 ('I was on my way when the rider cancelled') is a statement, not a system record, and it does not establish any entitlement to the fee; under the record-precedence rule it cannot carry a fee claim and the other side will use F8 to show I never even alleged a no-show.
The fee was in fact charged to the rider (F5), so a finding for the rider produces a real $6.61 refund — my case rests entirely on NS-4's 3-minute rule being applied to F2's 1:40 timing.

points.response: Agreed on characterisation: with the rider cancelling 1 min 40 s after acceptance (F2), the fee cannot be a driver no-show entitlement under NS-1/NS-6; it can only be tested under NS-0/NS-4, which I already argued in C1.

This point is mine, not a concession: NS-4 charges nothing for a rider cancellation within 3 minutes of matching, and F2 records cancellation at 12:55:40, 1 min 40 s after the 12:54:00 acceptance, so the $6.61 (F5) is unauthorised and refundable in full.
I do not need the driver's lateness to make the fee unauthorised — NS-4 fails on the 1:40 timing alone (F2); F3 and F1 only reinforce that no arrival-based charge exists here.
Conceded as far as it goes: F4 and F3 confirm no 'I'm Here' tap and no recorded arrival, so the driver has no waiting-time or no-show entitlement and the retained $6.61 (F5) must be returned.
F1 is agreed: 2,138 m closest approach, never within 200 m, which is why NS-1 (ii) fails — it is a fact for the rider, not against the refund request.

Agreed there is no safety escalation on this record: F7 shows no chat and F8 is a plain en-route statement, so the case stays a fee-authorisation matter under NS-4 and no SAFE-1 escalation is requested.
No fraud finding is pressed against the driver personally; I rely on profile facts (F13) only as context, and my case stands on the system records F2, F4 and F5, which alone defeat the $6.61.
Conceded: the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (F2), which is inside the 3-minute window, so NS-4 gives no basis for the $6.61 and I do not defend it as an early-cancellation charge.

Not contested on entitlement: no 'I'm Here' tap and no automatic arrival are on record (F4), so NS-1(i) fails and no no-show fee can be sustained — my client never claimed one; my D4 already conceded this.
Accepted as a system record: F1 (2,138 m closest approach, never within 200 m) means NS-1(ii) is not satisfied; I lead this fact myself in D5 because it shows my client asserted no arrival-based fee.

Conceded: F3 (driver_arrived_at null) is a system record and, per the record-precedence rule, it beats my client's statement F8 ('I was on my way'), which proves only that he was en route, not that he arrived; F8 therefore cannot support any fee.

Conceded as to the outcome, with one correction of reasoning: the $6.61 must be refunded because the rider cancelled inside 3 minutes (F2) under NS-4, not on any FARE-1 theory — F6 shows no surge and F5 shows only the single fee, so nothing extra was billed beyond the fee itself.

Objected to: no flag can attach to my client here — NS-2's flag is triggered by a driver tapping 'I'm Here' while GPS shows him outside 200 m (F1, F3, F4 show he never tapped and was never inside 200 m), NS-4/NS-3 place no breach on the driver, and his clean record (5.0 years, 4.76 rating, 649 trips, 0 upheld disputes, F13) gives no basis for account review.

Supporting the record's completeness for human review: there is no chat at all (F7), no traffic incident on the route (F10), only a mid-speed band on one street (F9) and fair weather (F11), so the file contains no safety allegation and no justified-reroute issue requiring a person — it resolves cleanly on NS-4.

Unchanged: the rider's own profile (2 disputes in 90 d, 2 upheld, both no-show, F12) is noted but cannot decide this case, and it is not weighed against the refund the system records (F1, F3, F4) require.
